name: Calm
tagline: Organize user-owned relaxation audio, timers, and a private routine tracker

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Unlimited unguided timed meditations; Day 1 of every multi-day program; 1 guided breathing exercise; 1 named Sleep Story
tiers.notes: The number of free ambient scenes/sounds is not published.

tiers.name: Calm Premium
tiers.limits: Full meditation, music, and 500+ Sleep Stories catalog
tiers.notes: $79.99 billed annually; the direct web annual flow advertises a 14-day trial, while some app-store flows may use 7 days.

tiers.name: Calm Family
tiers.notes: Official support lists $99.99/year ($8.33/month equivalent), while a live Calm family marketing page simultaneously displayed $119.99/year ($10.00/month equivalent); the numeric field is null because Calm's own current pages conflict.

tiers.name: Calm Lifetime
tiers.limits: 1 account with lifetime access to Calm Premium content
tiers.notes: $499.99 one-time; generally nonrefundable and does not automatically cancel an existing recurring subscription.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Free access: unlimited unguided timers, Day 1 of every multi-day program, 1 guided breathing exercise, and 1 named Sleep Story; no published numeric cap for ambient scenes.
pricing.billingTerms: Premium monthly + annual; Family annual only; Lifetime one-time; annual web trial commonly 14 days
pricing.hiddenCosts: Family pricing conflicts across Calm's own live pages ($99.99 support vs $119.99 marketing). Buying Lifetime does not cancel an existing subscription, creating a double-billing risk; web annual trial converts to the full annual charge unless canceled.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Calm, organize user-owned relaxation audio, timers, and a private routine tracker. The hard boundary is large licensed content catalog, celebrity audio, production, mobile apps, and brand, plus hardware data, content, coaching, and trust.
coreLoopDIY: Organize user-owned relaxation audio and timers, log user-chosen wellbeing signals in a private routine tracker, plan moderate routines, and show trends without diagnosing, shaming, or enforcing restrictive goals.
requirements: optional HealthKit or Health Connect permission
whatYouLose: large licensed content catalog, celebrity audio, production, mobile apps, and brand
large content library and social network
moatNotes: hardware data, content, coaching, and trust
ongoingBurden: sensor permissions, data quality, notifications, safety language, accessibility, sync, privacy, content review, and support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Calm because people pay for polished mobile capture, trusted content, hardware integration, and coaching rather than the basic logbook. The recurring cost buys sensor permissions, data quality, notifications, safety language, accessibility, sync, privacy, content review, and support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: wger
priorArt.desc: Active open-source fitness and workout management application.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Medito
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Everything is genuinely free, but it plays Medito’s library rather than organizing your audio.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Calm Premium plan and a personal general-wellbeing tracker DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Calm in an empty repository.
Use React Native with Expo, TypeScript, SQLite, and HealthKit or Health Connect only when explicitly enabled; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: organize user-owned relaxation audio and timers, log user-chosen wellbeing signals in a private routine tracker, plan moderate routines, and show trends without diagnosing, shaming, or enforcing restrictive goals.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create optional logs for activity, sleep, mood, energy, and personal notes with editable units.
Let the user build moderate routines and rest days without weight-loss targets, punishment, or competitive pressure.
Request health-platform permissions per data type and work fully without granting them.
Show weekly patterns and consistency with neutral language and no diagnostic or body-image judgments.
Add reminders that can be muted, data export, account-free local use, and full deletion.
Include a clear statement that the app is not medical care and should not replace qualified advice.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out medical diagnosis or treatment.
Deliberately leave out extreme exercise or restrictive-eating coaching.
Deliberately leave out wearable hardware, human coaching, and a large social network.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
